Each serializer class in `Registry`, after `load_serializers`, declares the options `read` forwards to it (PR #466). A PROV-JSONLD class that dropped `parse_float` would go unnoticed without it, because no test passes that option to PROV-JSONLD through `read`. It reads the registry and calls no `read`, so it would sit as well in a serializer test module.

`ProvDocument.deserialize` opens a path in binary mode and decodes it as UTF-8, so a non-ASCII label written to a file reads back under the C locale, for PROV-N and PROV-JSON (PR #448, the 3.2.0 release review). Without it a text-mode open with no encoding would go unnoticed. It calls `ProvDocument.deserialize` and not `read`, so it would sit as well in a model test module.

`_resolve_source` reads a bytes source that names an existing file as a path, not as raw content (#239), and `ProvDocument.deserialize` opens it. A bytes source takes the `isinstance` and `isfile` branch of `_resolve_source`, where a `pathlib.Path` skips that branch, so the pair reach different code. The judge kept it apart from test_read.py::test_read_accepts_pathlib_path because merging adds lines and an import and hides each input behind a converter. The raw-content merge in test_read.py::test_read_accepts_raw_content differs, because there str and str.encode build one input that takes one branch.

A file object from open is passed on by `_resolve_source` and read through the stream branch of `ProvDocument.deserialize`, which recognises a stream by its read method (#240). It is the one test in test_read.py that fails if that branch is narrowed to `io.StringIO` and `io.BytesIO`, because test_read.py::test_read_explicit_format_with_broken_seekable_reaches_deserializer passes a `StringIO` subclass.

A `pathlib.Path` source is not a str or bytes, so `_resolve_source` leaves it as a path and `ProvDocument.deserialize` opens it, rather than reading it as raw content. The judge kept it apart from test_read.py::test_read_accepts_bytes_file_path because merging adds lines and an import and hides each input behind a converter. The raw-content merge in test_read.py::test_read_accepts_raw_content differs, because there str and str.encode build one input that takes one branch.

`_resolve_source` returns a str or bytes that names no file as raw content, which `ProvDocument.deserialize` reads with format="json" and `_detect_and_parse` reads with auto-detection (#239). Folds in test_read.py::test_read_accepts_raw_content_string_with_explicit_format, test_read.py::test_read_auto_detects_raw_content_string, test_read.py::test_read_accepts_raw_content_bytes_with_explicit_format and test_read.py::test_read_auto_detects_raw_content_bytes. str and str.encode only build the input and format=None is the default, so nothing was lost.

A truncated JSON document chains no cause, because the JSON parser's error is not a `ProvSerializationError` (#653). `_detect_and_parse` keeps each candidate's error, and without the type filter in `_rejection_cause` the `JSONDecodeError` would be chained.

Content that starts with < is PROV-XML or RDF/XML, so `_rejection_cause` names no reader and `_detect_and_parse` raises with no cause (PR #623). A rule that chained the PROV-XML reader's error for that content fails this test and no other in test_read.py.

A stream that is not seekable gets no start position from `_prepare_stream`, so the first candidate consumes it, `_head` has nothing left to name a reader by, and no cause is chained (#239, PR #623). It is the one test in the suite that fails if `_prepare_stream` ignores the stream's seekable answer, because the PROV-N reader is then reached and its error chained. It does not pin the start-position guard in `_head`, whose broad except returns None without that guard.

The rejected reader's error is the `__cause__` of `ProvFormatNotDetected`, for PROV-JSON, PROV-JSONLD and PROV-N content (PR #623, #653). `_head` reads content, a stream and a path by three branches, and the text and bytes streams differ in its final decode. The jsonld and provn stream rows also fail when `_prepare_stream` and `_detect_and_parse` stop rewinding between candidates. Each content names a different reader in `_rejection_cause`, except json-language-tag, whose error is a model `ProvValueError` that `_decode_record_group` wraps.

`_detect_and_parse` runs each candidate inside `collect_warnings`, so `warn` adds the warning of a candidate that fails or parses to an empty document to a list that is then dropped, and `read` emits none of them (PR #565). Folds in test_read.py::test_read_auto_detect_drops_a_failed_candidates_warnings and test_read.py::test_read_auto_detect_drops_an_empty_candidates_warnings. The bodies were the same apart from the patched candidate, which is an input, so nothing was lost.

`_detect_and_parse` replays the winner's collected warning once through `warn`, with its own category, and `external_stacklevel` attributes it to the file that called `read` (PR #565). A replay with the wrong stack level, a repeated replay or a lost category fails it. test_read.py::test_read_auto_detect_keeps_the_once_per_location_record checks the warnings registry across two reads instead.

The winner's warning, replayed through `warn`, is attributed by `external_stacklevel` to the module that called `read`, so a filter on that module name matches (PR #565). The wrong stack level that fails test_read.py::test_read_auto_detect_emits_the_winners_warnings_once_at_the_caller fails this test too. The judge kept it apart from test_read.py::test_read_auto_detect_raises_the_winners_warning_under_an_error_filter because a merge would hide the module filter, which is what this test adds to that one.

`_detect_and_parse` gives each candidate only the options its class declares, so `profile` with JSON content does not reach `ProvJSONSerializer` and the document still reads (PR #466). Without that filter the JSON candidate fails on the option, no candidate wins and `read` raises `ProvFormatNotDetected`.

It passed with and without the warning collection in `_detect_and_parse`. With the collection, `warn` only adds a losing candidate's warning to a list. Without it, the warning raised under the error filter is swallowed by the loop over candidates. The failed row of test_read.py::test_read_auto_detect_drops_a_non_winners_warnings gives `read` the same input, asserts the same result and records any replay of a loser's warning, so nothing was lost.

`_detect_and_parse` replays the winner's warning through `warn` and not through the standard library's warning call, so a `collect_warnings` opened around `read` receives it (PR #565). It is the one test in the suite that fails if the replay bypasses `warn` with the right stack level. No code in prov opens a collection around `read`, so the behaviour it pins belongs to the private warnings module.

Two reads from one line warn once, and an unrelated warning from the same test still shows, because the replay through `warn` warns at the location `external_stacklevel` gives and keeps the warnings registry's once-per-location record (PR #565). A replay that reset `__warningregistry__` or warned from a new location each time would go unnoticed without it.

A lenient PROV-N read through auto-detection warns about the unknown keyword and skips it, so the real reader's warning survives the collection in `_detect_and_parse` and reaches the caller through `warn` (PR #565). test_provn_profiles.py::test_lenient_warning_reports_the_read_call_site makes the same auto-detecting call and checks the warning's file, so a later audit of either module compares the two.

The winner's warning raises from `read` under a category error filter, because `_detect_and_parse` replays it through `warn` after the candidate's try block (PR #565). A replay inside the candidate's collection would go back into that collection and never reach the filter. The judge kept it apart from test_read.py::test_read_auto_detect_emits_under_the_callers_module_name because the pair pins two behaviours, the replay raises and the replay is attributed to the caller, and a merge would hide the module filter.

When every candidate fails, `_detect_and_parse` catches any exception, a `RuntimeError` included, and `read` raises `ProvFormatNotDetected` (#239). An except narrowed to prov's own errors would let the json candidate's `RuntimeError` escape. The cause is None because garbage content names no reader in `_rejection_cause`, not because of the except. The test does not patch `ProvJSONLDSerializer`, so that candidate fails with its own error.

When the stream's tell raises, `_prepare_stream` gives no start position and `_detect_and_parse` runs without rewinds, and PROV-JSON still reads because `ProvJSONSerializer` is the first candidate `load_serializers` registers (#239). Named protected in the rubric.

A seekable `StringIO` of PROV-XML auto-detects, because `_detect_and_parse` rewinds it before each candidate to the start `_prepare_stream` records, so the XML reader sees the whole document (#239). The judge kept it apart from test_read.py::test_read_auto_detects_xml_from_seekable_bytesio because merging adds a line and needs a pair of callables to rebuild each stream.

With a truthiness test on content in `ProvDocument.deserialize`, every candidate raises a `TypeError` of its own and the test still passes.

A stream whose seekable method raises still reads with a format, through `ProvDocument.deserialize`. `read` never calls `_prepare_stream` on the explicit-format path today, so the test guards against a later edit to `read` that probes the stream there.
